name: gzip
plain: `gzip` compresses a file to make it smaller and replaces it with a .gz file; gzip -d (or gunzip) expands it back. It compresses one file at a time; tar bundles many files and gzip compresses the bundle (.tar.gz).
In CTFs you meet .gz files, and data that is compressed inside other formats.
when: Read a compressed log without unpacking it (zcat, zgrep).
Check whether a .gz file is damaged (gzip -t).

examples.title: Compress a file  (keeps your original with -k)
examples.explain: Creates notes.txt.gz. Without -k the original file is replaced by the .gz file.

examples.title: Decompress  (-d)
examples.explain: Restores notes.txt and removes the .gz (add -k to keep it). gunzip is the same command.

examples.title: Read it without unpacking
examples.cmd: zcat notes.txt.gz | head -2; zgrep -i password notes.txt.gz
examples.explain: zcat prints the uncompressed text; zgrep searches inside the compressed file.

examples.title: Show details  (-l, -v)
examples.explain: Lists compressed and uncompressed sizes and the compression ratio.

examples.title: Test integrity  (-t)
examples.explain: Checks the file without unpacking. A damaged archive prints an error.

examples.title: Write to the screen  (-c)
examples.explain: -c sends the output to standard output and keeps the original. Good for pipelines and for measuring compressed size.

examples.title: Best or fastest compression  (-9, -1)
examples.cmd: gzip -9 -c notes.txt | wc -c; gzip -1 -c notes.txt | wc -c
examples.explain: Levels 1 to 9: faster and larger versus slower and smaller (--best and --fast are the same as 9 and 1).

options.plain: Write the result to standard output and keep the original file.
Keep the input file instead of deleting it.
Force: overwrite files, compress links, or write to a terminal.
List the compressed and uncompressed size and the ratio of a .gz file.
Test the integrity of a compressed file.
Show the name and compression percentage of each file.
Go into folders and process the files inside.
options.use: Compressing a whole tree (file by file).

options.plain: Do not save or restore the original file name and timestamp.
Save and restore the original file name and timestamp (the default when compressing).
Compression level: 1 is fastest, 9 is smallest; --fast is -1 and --best is -9.
Make the output friendlier to rsync by resetting compression at intervals.
Flush the output to disk after each write.

mistakes: gzip replaces the original file by default: use -k or -c if you want to keep it.
gzip compresses single files: for folders use tar -czf.
A .gz file can hide another format inside; run file on the result.
gzip -d on a file without the .gz suffix fails: name it .gz or use -S or -c.
try: Compress a log, read it with zcat, then unpack it.
Compare the compressed size at -1 and -9.
Use file on a .gz and on its contents to see both layers.
see_also: gunzip(1), zcat(1), zgrep(1), tar(1), bzip2(1), xz(1), zip(1), file(1).
captured_with: Examples are written to explain a technique; they are not captured output.
